what_it_does: The paper addresses the high energy consumption in high-performance computing (HPC) systems, which strains electrical grids. It proposes using machine learning large language models (LLMs) to predict how much power each computing job will consume before it runs. A lightweight scheduling strategy is developed to manage job execution based on these predictions. The approach integrates into Slurm, the widely-used job scheduler for HPC clusters, without requiring deep changes to the core system.
